title: Exchange-stable Ds states span both margin regimes; ascent selects the funnel at scale
statement: Exact full-lattice census (N = 10..14, K = 3, centered06 + mix3 grid laws) finds one-point exchange-stable profiled-Ds states plentiful (5-944 per instance, correcting the pre-audit 18-944 range) and overwhelmingly non-global. On the centered law their nuisance blocks span 1e-5 to 0.57 with value gap and nuisance block anti-correlated (-0.27 to -0.83 per instance); margin-retaining non-global stable states occur in every census instance at a Theta(1) price, and near-coincident projected centroids occur, so (M5) must be checked. The efficient-score DP interval labeling is unstable in 7/10 centered instances (already N = 8, exact gain 0.447) and stable in 9/10 mix3 instances. Small-N ascent is seed-dependent. In the researcher library runs at N = 100/300/1000 every tested seed on the centered law terminates with nuisance at K/N scale and near-optimal value; 0.004-0.046 is an aggregate reported gap summary, not a run-wise bound. An independent N = 100 run reproduced stability and collapse for all three seeds but observed a random-seed gap 0.075. On mix3 the independent runs retained lambda_min about 1.7 with gaps below 7e-5. These are measured observations, not an asymptotic selection theorem.
assumptions: grid-law emulations (atomic), deterministic researcher seeds 20260830 + 1000N + rep; independent audit seeds and exact provenance are in AUDITS/artifacts/AUDIT-DS-STABLE-MARGINS-COMPILE-001
measured, never theorem authority; the asymptotic selection law is open (OPEN-DS-STABLE-BASINS)

proof_location.section: DS16. Margin price at arbitrary labelings, the value funnel, and the profiled compile verdict

role: the selection-effects evidence separating properties of stable states from properties of the seeding (packet blocker 5)
warning: Audit-hardened measured claim. The stable-count range is 5-944. The 0.004-0.046 researcher gap range is aggregate, not a universal per-run range; an independent N=100 random seed produced 0.075. Atomic grid laws and finite optimizer runs do not prove asymptotic basin selection.
